```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Small presentation helpers (formatting only; no computation of results).
kbl_house <- function(df, caption, digits = 2) {
  knitr::kable(df, caption = caption, digits = digits, align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(df) - 1))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = TRUE) |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
}
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
has <- function(x) exists(x, envir = .GlobalEnv)
show_fig <- function(name) {
  if (has("figure_objects") && !is.null(figure_objects[[name]])) print(figure_objects[[name]])
  else cat("*Figure not available — run 05_FIGURES_TABLES_BOTH.R first.*\n")
}

# Inline value helpers for the explanatory text (read saved objects; '[n/a]' if missing).
NA_TXT <- "[n/a]"
row_of <- function(est, blk, vis, desc) {
  if (!has("primary_objects")) return(NULL)
  r <- primary_objects$summary[primary_objects$summary$estimand == est & primary_objects$summary$block == blk &
                               as.character(primary_objects$summary$visit) == vis & primary_objects$summary$descriptor == desc, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 1) r else NULL
}
ev <- function(est, blk, vis, desc, d = 1, ci = TRUE) {      # estimate (95% CI); E2 on ratio scale
  r <- row_of(est, blk, vis, desc); if (is.null(r)) return(NA_TXT)
  f <- if (grepl("^E2", est)) exp else identity
  if (!ci) return(fmt(f(r$estimate), d))
  sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s to %s)", fmt(f(r$estimate), d), fmt(f(r$ci_low), d), fmt(f(r$ci_high), d))
}
pct_more <- function(vis, desc, blk = "cumulative") {         # ratio -> "+x %"
  r <- row_of("E2", blk, vis, desc); if (is.null(r)) return(NA_TXT)
  sprintf("%+.0f %%", 100 * (exp(r$estimate) - 1))
}
dv <- function(obj, path, filt, col, d = 0, scale = 1) {     # generic descriptive lookup
  if (!has(obj)) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- get(obj, envir = .GlobalEnv)[[path]]
  for (k in names(filt)) x <- x[as.character(x[[k]]) == filt[[k]], , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(x) != 1) return(NA_TXT)
  fmt(scale * x[[col]], d)
}
c3_range <- function(col, min_mg, scale = 1) {                # range over bins >= min_mg, all visits
  if (!has("descriptive_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- descriptive_objects$c3; v <- scale * x[[col]][x$intensity >= min_mg]
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]; if (!length(v)) return(NA_TXT)
  paste0(fmt(min(v), 0), "–", fmt(max(v), 0))
}
pow_range <- function(scn) {                                  # detection % range over visits
  if (!has("validation_objects") || !"n_bins" %in% names(validation_objects$power_summary)) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- validation_objects$power_summary; v <- x$pct_detected[as.character(x$scenario) == scn]
  if (!length(v)) return(NA_TXT)
  if (length(unique(round(v))) == 1) fmt(v[1], 0) else paste0(fmt(min(v), 0), "–", fmt(max(v), 0))
}
sim_txt <- function() {
  if (!has("validation_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  s <- validation_objects$settings; sprintf("%d datasets x %d bootstrap replicates per scenario and visit", s$N_SIM, s$B_SIM)
}
tip_lo <- function(blk, desc, raw = FALSE) {                   # delta at which the M18 lower 95% bound reaches 0
  r <- row_of("E1", blk, "M18", desc)
  if (is.null(r) || !has("sensitivity_objects")) return(if (raw) NA_real_ else NA_TXT)
  s9 <- sensitivity_objects$s9; s9 <- s9[s9$block == blk & s9$descriptor == desc, ][1, ]
  v <- r$ci_low / (s9$n_m18_imputed / s9$n_with_m0)
  if (raw) v else fmt(v, 1)
}
null_txt <- function() {
  if (!has("validation_objects") || !"any_bump_mc95" %in% names(validation_objects$power_summary)) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- validation_objects$power_summary; x <- x[as.character(x$scenario) == "null (true null)", ]
  paste(sprintf("%s %.1f%% (MC 95%% CI %s%%)", x$visit, x$pct_any_bump, x$any_bump_mc95), collapse = "; ")
}
# A07 revision helpers (formatting only).
show_rev <- function(obj, name) {
  if (has(obj) && !is.null(get(obj, envir = .GlobalEnv)$figs[[name]])) print(get(obj, envir = .GlobalEnv)$figs[[name]])
  else cat("*Figure not available — run the revision scripts 07-09 first.*\n")
}
conc_v <- function(vis, desc, col, d = 0, set = NULL) {      # value from the revised concentration table
  if (!has("rev_AB_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- rev_AB_objects$conc; x <- x[as.character(x$visit) == vis & x$descriptor == desc, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(set)) x <- x[x$set == set, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(x) != 1 || !is.finite(x[[col]])) return(NA_TXT)
  fmt(x[[col]], d)
}
conc_ci <- function(vis, desc, col, d = 0) {                  # "x (95% CI a-b)"
  if (!has("rev_AB_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s–%s)", conc_v(vis, desc, col, d), conc_v(vis, desc, paste0(col, "_ci_low"), d),
          conc_v(vis, desc, paste0(col, "_ci_high"), d))
}
conc_range <- function(col, lo, hi, d = 0) {                  # range over bins with lo <= lower_mg < hi, all visits
  if (!has("rev_AB_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- rev_AB_objects$conc; v <- x[[col]][x$set == "bin" & x$lower_mg >= lo & x$lower_mg < hi]
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]; if (!length(v)) return(NA_TXT)
  paste0(fmt(min(v), d), "–", fmt(max(v), d))
}
shape_v <- function(contrast, col, d = 2, sample = "all") {
  if (!has("rev_CD_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- rev_CD_objects$shape_summary; x <- x[x$contrast == contrast & grepl(paste0("^", sample), x$sample), ]
  if (nrow(x) != 1) return(NA_TXT)
  fmt(x[[col]], d)
}
ev_rev <- function(outcome, model, severity, sample, visit, contrast, d = 2) {   # model contrast with CI
  if (!has("rev_E_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- rev_E_objects$models
  x <- x[as.character(x$outcome) == outcome & x$model == model & x$severity == severity & x$sample == sample &
         x$visit == visit & x$contrast == contrast, ]
  if (nrow(x) != 1) return(NA_TXT)
  sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s to %s)", fmt(x$estimate, d), fmt(x$ci_low, d), fmt(x$ci_high, d))
}
claim_ok <- function(pattern) {                                # statement check from 10_REV_VALIDATION
  if (!has("rev_validation_objects")) return(NA)
  x <- rev_validation_objects$claims; isTRUE(all(x$holds[grepl(pattern, x$claim, fixed = TRUE)]))
}
inner_set <- function(est, blk, vis, delta = 0) {
  if (!has("primary_objects")) return(NA_TXT)
  x <- primary_objects$conf_sets
  x <- x[x$estimand == est & x$block == blk & as.character(x$visit) == vis & abs(x$delta - delta) < 1e-6, ]
  if (nrow(x) == 1) paste(x$inner_set, "mg") else NA_TXT
}
```

<div class="warning-box">

**Caution:** The simultaneous bands behind these sets are not separately calibrated per bin. The true-null simulation calibrates the ≥2-bin bump rule only. Treat the M18 sets (n = 39) with particular caution.

## Key messages for the clinical reader {.unnumbered}

<div class="note-box">

These messages describe the full run of 2026-10-14 (B = 2000; the master md5 is in the reproducibility appendix), revised on 2026-10-16 (A07; scripts 07–10, B = 2000). Messages 4–6 changed in the revision; messages 1–3 and 7 are unchanged.
- Estimates, CIs, ranges and percentages are computed from the saved results when the report is knitted.
- The qualitative wording was checked against that run. If the analysis is re-run on a different input, re-check that the wording still matches the numbers.

</div>

1. **Patients become clearly more active, and the gain is still present at M18.**
   - Time above 100 mg rose by `r ev("E1","cumulative","M3","T100")` min/day at M3 and by `r ev("E1","cumulative","M6","T100")` min/day at M6.
   - It was still `r ev("E1","cumulative","M18","T100")` min/day higher at M18. This M18 estimate assumes missing-at-random, and dropout to M18 is informative (see the tipping-point analysis).
   - The baseline median was `r dv("qc_objects","profiles",list(kind="cumulative",visit_code="M0",descriptor="T100"),"median")` min/day, so these are relative increases of `r pct_more("M3","T100")`, `r pct_more("M6","T100")` and `r pct_more("M18","T100")`.

2. **No evidence of a specific intensity band carrying the change.** The daily intensity distribution tilts smoothly towards higher accelerations:
   - the share of the day spent below 20 mg falls;
   - low-intensity bins (below ~100 mg) lose relative share;
   - higher-intensity bins gain relative share, the more so the higher the intensity.

   The pre-specified shape test found no localised departure at any visit, and the result was unchanged in every invariance check.

   What the test can and cannot see (true-null simulation, `r sim_txt()`):
   - False alarms under a true null are rare: `r null_txt()`.
   - A localised extra gain of about +22% would very likely have been detected, whether narrow or broad: `r pow_range("2 bins 120-160, +0.2")` % for 2 bins at 120–160 mg and `r pow_range("6 bins 70-140, +0.2")` % for 6 bins at 70–140 mg.
   - A smaller extra gain (+10%) could have been missed, especially at M18: detection was `r pow_range("2 bins 120-160, +0.1")` % for 2 bins and `r pow_range("6 bins 70-140, +0.1")` % for 6 bins, and small broad departures may be flagged in the wrong place (mislocalised).

3. **Where minutes are gained and where the relative change is largest are different places.**
   - *Absolute* gain is certainly positive from about 80–90 mg upwards and is largest, in minutes, up to ~140 mg, where most active time is spent.
   - Similar point estimates below 80 mg are too imprecise to be distinguished from zero.
   - The *relative* increase is largest at high intensities: for example ×`r ev("E2","bins","M3","300-325",2,FALSE)` at 300–325 mg at M3. In absolute terms these are fractions of a minute per day.

4. **Early and later follow-up may differ (hypothesis).**
   - At M3 the relative gain at the highest intensities is largest: ×`r ev("E2","bins","M3","375-400",2,FALSE)` at 375–400 mg. It is smaller at M6 and M18 (×`r ev("E2","bins","M6","375-400",2,FALSE)` and ×`r ev("E2","bins","M18","375-400",2,FALSE)`).
   - This is compatible with an early "burst" of more vigorous movement that settles into a mid-range increase.
   - It is a hypothesis, for three reasons:
     - the formal paired comparisons of the shape of change (new in A07) find no tilt difference between any visits. The overall shape differs nominally only for M6 vs M3 (p = `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","p_wald_boot",3)`), and not after Holm adjustment (`r shape_v("M6 minus M3","p_wald_boot_holm",3)`);
     - M3 and M6 overlap in timing (2–6 vs 5–9 months);
     - the visits differ in season contrast (no M0→M6 pair falls in the same season).

5. **Response is broad in direction but unequal in size (revised in A07).**
   - Between `r conc_range("pct_positive", 70, 400)` % of patients gain time in a given bin from 70 mg upwards; in the lowest bins it is about half.
   - The 10 % of patients with the largest gains contribute `r conc_range("share_pos", 60, 400)` % of all *positive* gains from 60 mg upwards (the minimum possible, if all gains were equal, is about 13–21 %). Concentration is of similar size across the spectrum; at M3 it is numerically higher above ~240 mg, but intervals overlap and this was not tested formally.
   - The first report's figure of 46–75 % "of the total gain above 200 mg" used the *net* gain as denominator. Above 200 mg that gives values only moderately above the positive-gain share, but the net estimand is undefined or exceeds 100 % (up to `r if (has("rev_AB_objects")) fmt(max(rev_AB_objects$conc$share_net_orig, na.rm = TRUE), 0) else NA_TXT` %) where gains and losses cancel, so the positive-gain share is now the primary heterogeneity measure.

6. **Subtypes (exploratory; adjusted models added in A07).**
   - IMNM gains less time above 100 mg than DM (`r ev_rev("dT100","E_b_sev","ph_vas","complete ph_vas","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)` min/day averaged over visits, adjusted for ph_VAS). Adjusting for baseline muscle strength (MMT8) hardly changes the point estimate within the same patients (`r ev_rev("dT100","E_a_unadjusted","mmt8","complete mmt8","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)` unadjusted vs `r ev_rev("dT100","E_b_sev","mmt8","complete mmt8","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)` adjusted), but the interval widens to include 0; MMT8 itself is not associated with ΔT100.
   - There is no evidence of a subtype difference in the *shape* of change (tilt, ΔIG), but the intervals are wide.
   - ph_VAS is substantially driven by extramuscular activity in DM and ASyS but almost purely by muscle activity in IMNM, so it is an imperfect adjustment for initial muscle impairment.
   - With 12–18 pairs per subtype and visit and no multiplicity control, these are hypotheses for an adequately powered study.

7. **Practical consequence.**
   - The data **do not support a new IIM-specific intensity cut-point**.
   - Time above a conventional threshold (e.g. 100 mg) and mean ENMO describe the volume of change.
   - The intensity gradient (IG) is a closely related, cut-point-free summary of the tilt. It tracks the patient-level tilt only moderately (ρ ≈ `r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M6"),"spearman_slope_vs_d_ig",2)` at M6), and its group-level time course differs, so it is a reasonable but not equivalent summary.


<div class="note-box">

**How to read this report.**

- Three questions are answered separately, each by its own pre-specified estimand:
  - **E1:** where time is gained, in absolute minutes/day per 10 mg;
  - **E2:** where the relative increase is largest, as a ratio of means;
  - **E3:** whether the *shape* of the intensity distribution changes beyond a smooth shift.
- Only E3 can support a claim of a specific informative interval.
- The location of a maximum depends on the estimand, so maxima are not presented as cut-points.

</div>

# Revision A07: what changed {.tabset}

## Summary {.unnumbered}

<div class="note-box">

The revision addressed five proposals (A–E) of `MYO_A07_narhy_na_zmeny.txt`. Each was first assessed for statistical justification; the decisions are in `docs/261016_A07_critical_review.md`.

- **Unchanged:** the primary analysis, its estimands (E1–E4), populations, thresholds, bin definitions, models and all their numbers. They are reproduced to 10⁻⁶ by the validation script (R9).
- **Changed:** the descriptive profile figure (A), the heterogeneity estimand and its interpretation (B), and the explanation of the shape figure (C).
- **Added:** robustness checks of the shape test (C), paired visit comparisons (D) and exploratory severity-adjusted subtype models using clinical data from outside the master (E).

</div>

```{r tab_changelog}
  "Validation", "added", "script 10 (R1-R10)", "see validation tab"
) |> kbl_house("Change log of revision A07")
```

# Research questions and estimands

| Code | Question | Estimand | Analysis set |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Where in the spectrum is time gained? | Δ mean min/day per 10 mg, Mx − M0 (MMRM, unstructured covariance) | all measurements (MAR) |
| E2 | Where is the relative change largest? | ratio of marginal means Mx/M0 from the same MMRM | all measurements (MAR) |
| E3 | Does the shape change beyond a smooth shift? | mean paired clr change of a 21-part 24-h composition; residual from a natural-spline null in log intensity | complete pairs |
| E4 | Is change large relative to its variability? | dz = mean Δ / SD(Δ) | complete pairs |
| CUM | Complementary overlapping representation | E1/E2 for 24 cumulative thresholds | all measurements |

Estimable with these data:

- group-level change (E1/E2);
- precision of the group-level change (bootstrap SE);
- exposure prevalence (coverage).

**Not estimable** from the master dataset:

- individual test-retest reliability (ICC/SEM/SDC). This needs GGIR day-level output (`part2_daysummary`);
- clinical predictive value, which is out of scope.

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** How many recordings and patients enter the analysis.

</div>

```{r qc_table}
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**How to read.**

- Every row is an automatic consistency check on the master dataset.
- **PASS** means the data obey the expected arithmetic. For example, time in an exclusive bin equals the difference of the two neighbouring cumulative thresholds, and time above a higher threshold is never larger than time above a lower one.
- **WARN** marks features that do not invalidate the data but must be considered in interpretation: patients without baseline, recordings with fewer than 5 valid days, overlapping M3/M6 timing windows, and undefined subtype codes.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.** There are no FAIL results, so the data are internally consistent and the derived exclusive bins are exact.

**Clinically relevant WARN: visit timing.**

- M3 was recorded 2–6 months after M0 and M6 4–9 months after M0, so the two windows partly overlap.
- "M3 vs M6" differences should therefore be read as *early vs later follow-up*, not as exact 3- and 6-month time points.
- A sensitivity analysis using the actual time since baseline gave the same picture.

</div>


```{r patterns}
if (has("qc_objects")) {
  kbl_house(qc_objects$visit_patterns |> dplyr::rename(`Visit pattern` = pattern, Patients = n_patients),
            "Observed visit patterns (main visits)", 0)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** Which visits each patient contributed. Only about half of the patients have all four main visits.

**Why it matters.** The mixed model (MMRM) uses every available measurement and remains valid when missingness depends on what was already observed (MAR). The simpler paired comparisons (M0 vs Mx) use only patients with both visits.

</div>


```{r fig_desc, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
show_rev("rev_AB_objects", "A1")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows (revised, A07-A).**

- The daily intensity profile **per 10 mg of bin width**: median minutes per day per 10 mg within each exclusive bin (line) and the 10th–90th percentile range (band), separately for each visit.
- Each recording is normalised (minutes in bin × 10 / bin width) before summarising. Native GGIR bins are 10 mg wide up to 120 mg, 20 mg up to 300 mg and 25 mg up to 400 mg (dotted lines).
- The y-axis is compressed (log 1 + x) so that the few minutes at high intensity remain visible next to the hours at low intensity.

</div>

```{r fig_desc_compare, fig.width=14, fig.height=7}
show_rev("rev_AB_objects", "A2")
```

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- The original figure (panel A, unchanged from the first report) plotted minutes *within* bins of unequal width. Its local rise at 120–140 mg is created entirely by the doubling of bin width from 10 to 20 mg. The raw median rises at 120–140 mg at every visit (`r if (isTRUE(claim_ok("raw profile rises"))) "confirmed" else "[check]"`).
- After normalisation (panel B) the median profile **decreases monotonically with intensity at every visit** (`r if (isTRUE(claim_ok("decrease monotonically"))) "no increase between any adjacent bins" else "[check]"`). There is no local peak.
- The change of shape is fully explained by the normalisation factor. Normalised quantiles equal raw quantiles × 10 / width in every bin and visit, and the raw values reproduce the original table exactly (validation R2, R9b).
- Time falls steeply with intensity: most of the day is spent below 100 mg, and above ~250 mg typical patients accumulate well under one minute per day per 10 mg.
- The follow-up curves (M3, M6, M18) lie slightly but consistently above the baseline curve (M0, dot-dash) from roughly 70 mg upwards. This anticipates the main result: a broad upward shift rather than a single peak.

</div>


<div class="warning-box">

**Caution:** Missing visits are not missing completely at random.

- Patients who later lack M18 tended to have larger M3 gains (S10).
- E1/E2 therefore use MMRM, which is valid under MAR. The M18 estimate is additionally stress-tested with a delta-adjusted tipping-point analysis (S9).
- Reasons for missing M0/M18 are not recorded in the master dataset.

</div>

---

# Statistical methods, alternative models and independent review {.tabset}

## Models {.unnumbered}

**E1 and E2.** For each exclusive bin, and separately for each cumulative threshold, minutes/day are modelled with a mixed model for repeated measures:

- visit (M0, M3, M6, M18) is a fixed factor with an unstructured patient-level covariance (glmmTMB, REML);
- the outcome is scaled by its SD for numerical stability and back-transformed.

E1 is the visit contrast in min/day per 10 mg of bin width. E2 is the ratio of model-based marginal means (β₀ + βₓ)/β₀. When the unstructured model does not converge, a random-intercept model is used; such fallbacks are logged.

**E3.** Each recording is represented as a 21-part 24-h composition: <20 mg, 19 bins from 20 to 300 mg, and ≥300 mg. Zeros are replaced multiplicatively by 0.65 × one 5-s epoch per recording. The analysis then proceeds in three steps:

1. Mean paired changes in centred log-ratios are computed for every part.
2. For the bounded bins, these changes are regressed on log geometric-mean intensity with a natural spline (df = 3), which serves as the smooth null.
3. The residuals are the shape-departure estimand.

**Uncertainty.** A patient-level cluster bootstrap provides all intervals:

- one set of patient draws is shared by all estimands, bins, thresholds and visits;
- duplicated patients receive new cluster IDs, and the draws are pre-generated, so results do not depend on the number of workers.

From the bootstrap, the report shows pointwise percentile intervals and simultaneous 95% bands (max-t over the bins of a visit). Inner and outer confidence sets are derived from those bands.

## Decision rule {.unnumbered}

A **localised informative interval** is reported only when both hold:

- E3 residuals show a *bump*: at least 2 contiguous bins whose simultaneous band excludes zero, bounded on both sides by bins that do not, and touching neither grid edge;
- the bump is invariant to the zero-replacement value (epoch, 0.01, 0.5 min/day), to restricting to ≥5 valid days, and to excluding the UCTD/SSc patient.

Otherwise the report states that there is **no evidence of a localised departure**. It then adds either that the change is a smooth redistribution towards higher intensities (when the linear tilt is non-zero) or that shape change is not identifiable.

Coverage and magnitude are reported as separate descriptive dimensions, not as gates.

## Independent review {.unnumbered}

The plan was reviewed by a different model (Claude Fable 5.1). There were two review rounds, both with the verdict REVISE, and every objection was dispositioned:

- the full review: `docs/261013_phase3_independent_review.md`;
- the point-by-point disposition and locked plan v2: `docs/261013_phase3_disposition_and_locked_plan.md`.

Key changes:

- the claim that the high-intensity response is an SD artefact was withdrawn;
- E1 was normalised per 10 mg;
- E2 was made MAR;
- the shape estimand E3 with a smooth null was introduced;
- the gating decision rule was replaced by confidence sets;
- sliding windows were dropped.

## Revision A07 {.unnumbered}

*Independent review of the revision:* Claude Fable 5.1, verdict MINOR REVISION (no critical findings; three major findings on interpretation, all addressed). See `docs/261016_A07_independent_review.md` and the disposition in `docs/261016_A07_validation_change_log_summary.md` §5.


The revision follows `MYO_A07_narhy_na_zmeny.txt`. The full point-by-point assessment (accepted / modified / rejected, with justification) is in `docs/261016_A07_critical_review.md`. The original scripts 01–06 and the original report are unchanged; the revision adds scripts 07–10.

**A — Descriptive profile per 10 mg.** Each recording's minutes within a bin are multiplied by 10 / bin width (10, 20 or 25 mg) *before* the median and P10–P90 are computed. Because the width is constant within a bin, this is numerically identical to rescaling the summaries; no synthetic 10-mg bins are interpolated.

**B — Concentration of change.** In every bin and visit (complete pairs), the "top 10 %" are the k = ceiling(0.1 × n) patients with the largest change, where n counts *all* pairs of the cell. Three different quantities are reported:

- **% of patients with a gain** (change > 0);
- **positive-gain concentration** (new): the sum of the k largest *positive* gains divided by the sum of all positive gains. Its reference value if all gains were equal is min(k, n₊)/n₊;
- **share of the net gain** (original): sum of the k largest changes divided by the sum of all changes. It is undefined when the net change ≤ 0 and unstable when gains and losses nearly cancel, so it is shown together with the *net/gross index* Σ change / Σ |change|. Cells with an index below 0.20 are flagged as unstable.

Ties at the k-th value do not change the sums. Intervals come from the same patient-level cluster bootstrap as the primary analysis (B = 2000, seed 20261013).

**C — Robustness of the shape test (E3).** The paired clr change minus a smooth trend is algebraically invariant to the per-10-mg normalisation and to the clr centre. Both add constants that the spline intercept absorbs, and this is confirmed numerically. Bin width therefore enters E3 only through the position of the bins on the log-intensity axis and through their resolution. Tested variants:

- smooth null with df = 1 (linear), 2, 4 and 5;
- a fit weighted by each bin's log-width;
- a uniform 20-mg grid (resolution change);
- bounded bins up to 400 mg (composition-range change).

A plasmode simulation compares false-alarm rates and power for df = 2–5, including a mis-specified null in which the true smooth profile has df = 5.

**D — Do the shapes of change differ between follow-up visits?** In patients with M0 and both visits, the paired difference of clr change profiles is evaluated three ways: bin by bin with a max-t band; as a difference of the linear tilt; and by a 3-df bootstrap Wald test that the smooth difference curve is flat. P-values are Holm-adjusted over the three visit pairs. A sensitivity analysis uses the common sample with all four visits.

**E — Subtypes with baseline severity (exploratory).** Baseline clinical variables come from `klinicka_data_12102026.xlsx`, which is outside the master dataset. Random-intercept models of change from M0 are fitted for three pre-specified summaries (ΔT100, patient-level clr tilt, ΔIG), with `visit × subtype` (DM reference) and centred baseline severity. Severity is ph_VAS per 10 mm (primary, per the study team's decision) or MMT8 per 5 points (sensitivity). Further variants add severity × visit or the baseline value of the outcome. Contrasts carry patient-level cluster-bootstrap CIs (B = 2000); likelihood-ratio tests use ML fits.

# Results — CUMULATIVE thresholds

```{r fig_f1c, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
show_fig("F1c_E1_cumulative")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- How many more minutes per day patients spend *above* each threshold T at follow-up compared with M0, with 95% CI (shaded) and a simultaneous band (thin lines).
- "Above 100 mg" corresponds to the conventional GGIR "MVPA" threshold. This label is not a validated moderate-intensity category in myositis.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- The gain is largest at low thresholds: above 40 mg, `r ev("E1","cumulative","M3","T40")` min/day at M3. It decreases steadily with the threshold, because every higher threshold contains less time.
- Above 100 mg the gain is `r ev("E1","cumulative","M3","T100",1,FALSE)` and `r ev("E1","cumulative","M6","T100",1,FALSE)` min/day at M3 and M6, and `r ev("E1","cumulative","M18","T100",1,FALSE)` min/day at M18.
- Above 200 mg it is still `r ev("E1","cumulative","M3","T200")` min/day at M3.

**Why it is interesting.**

- The gain above 100 mg is about a third more such time than at baseline (baseline median `r dv("qc_objects","profiles",list(kind="cumulative",visit_code="M0",descriptor="T100"),"median")` min/day).
- It is still present at M18, under the missing-at-random assumption (see the tipping-point analysis).
- Whether a change of this size is clinically meaningful in IIM has not been established. That would need anchoring to function (for example MMT8, FI2, HAQ), which is outside the scope of this report.

</div>

<div class="warning-box">

**Caution:** Thresholds overlap: T100 contains everything above 100 mg, including the time above 200 mg. The curve therefore cannot tell *where* the change happens; the exclusive bins below answer that.

</div>

```{r fig_f2c, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
show_fig("F2c_E2_cumulative")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** The same comparison on a *relative* scale: follow-up time above T divided by M0 time above T (1 = no change). The y-axis is logarithmic.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- Above 20 mg the relative change is small (`r pct_more("M3","T20")` at M3), because almost the whole waking day is above 20 mg.
- The relative gain at M3 rises with the threshold:
  - `r pct_more("M3","T100")` above 100 mg;
  - `r pct_more("M3","T200")` above 200 mg;
  - `r pct_more("M3","T300")` above 300 mg.
- The more intense the movement, the larger the *proportional* increase, even though the number of minutes involved is small.

</div>

<div class="note-box">

**Note:** Cumulative thresholds are a complementary representation and are not used for localisation.

</div>

# Results — exclusive BINS

```{r fig_f1, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
show_fig("F1_E1_bins")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- The absolute change in minutes per day spent *within* each non-overlapping intensity bin, per 10 mg of bin width.
- Bins are 10, 20 or 25 mg wide; per-10 mg values make them comparable.
- **How to read:** an estimate of 2.5 at 90–100 mg means that patients spend on average 2.5 more minutes per day in that 10-mg slice of intensity than at baseline.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- At M3 and M6, point estimates of the absolute gain are roughly 1.5–3 min/day per 10 mg from ~40 mg up to ~120 mg, tapering towards 200 mg.
  - 90–100 mg: `r ev("E1","bins","M3","90-100")` at M3 and `r ev("E1","bins","M6","90-100")` at M6.
- The simultaneous band excludes zero only from about 80–90 mg upwards: `r inner_set("E1","bins","M3")` at M3 and `r inner_set("E1","bins","M6")` at M6.
- Below that, gains of similar size cannot be distinguished from zero. Low-intensity time varies far more between and within patients: the bootstrap SE is about 1.3–1.9 at 40–70 mg against about 0.8 at 90–100 mg.
- The lower edge of the "certain" range therefore reflects precision as much as the size of the change.
- At M18 the point estimates in the lowest bins (20–50 mg) are negative, but their CIs include zero, so no conclusion is possible there.

</div>

<div class="warning-box">

**Caution:** The 20–50 mg range in a 0–24 h analysis also contains restless sleep and very light movement. Changes there should not be interpreted as a change in a particular type of daytime activity.

</div>

```{r fig_f2, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
show_fig("F2_E2_bins")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- The relative change within each bin: the ratio of mean minutes at follow-up to M0, from the same model (1 = no change).
- The last point (≥ 400 mg) is time above the top of the measured grid, so the dotted line marks where the measurement scale ends.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- Below ~60 mg there is no relative change (ratio ≈ 1).
- From ~70 mg the ratio rises with intensity. At M3:
  - ×`r ev("E2","bins","M3","100-110",2,FALSE)` at 100–110 mg;
  - ×`r ev("E2","bins","M3","200-220",2,FALSE)` at 200–220 mg;
  - ×`r ev("E2","bins","M3","300-325",2,FALSE)` at 300–325 mg.
- At M6 and M18 the high-intensity ratios are smaller, about ×1.3–1.7.
- The simultaneous band excludes 1 over `r inner_set("E2","bins","M6")` at M6 and only over `r inner_set("E2","bins","M18")` at M18.
- There is no peak followed by a decline that would mark an "optimal band". The curve rises and then plateaus.

**Why it is interesting.**

- Time in the highest intensity bins roughly *doubles* in the early follow-up, but from a very low baseline of a few minutes per week per bin.
- This may reflect regained capacity for short, more demanding bouts of movement. Wrist ENMO has not been validated against activity type in IIM, so the kind of activity cannot be named.
- The upper limit of this effect cannot be determined because the GGIR grid ends at 400 mg.

</div>

```{r tab_e1e2}
if (has("primary_objects")) {
  primary_objects$summary |>
    dplyr::filter(estimand %in% c("E1", "E2"), block == "bins") |>
    dplyr::mutate(est = ifelse(estimand == "E2", exp(estimate), estimate),
                  lo = ifelse(estimand == "E2", exp(ci_low), ci_low), hi = ifelse(estimand == "E2", exp(ci_high), ci_high)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Bin = descriptor, Estimand = estimand, Visit = visit,
                     Estimate = fmt(est), `95% CI` = paste0(fmt(lo), " to ", fmt(hi)),
                     `Simult. band` = paste0(fmt(ifelse(estimand == "E2", exp(band_low), band_low)), " to ",
                                             fmt(ifelse(estimand == "E2", exp(band_high), band_high)))) |>
    kbl_house("E1 (min/day per 10 mg) and E2 (ratio of means) per exclusive bin")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**How to read.**

- E1 rows give minutes/day per 10 mg; E2 rows give the ratio of means.
- "Simult. band" is the conservative interval that keeps 95% coverage across all bins of a visit simultaneously. Use it when making statements about *which* bins changed.

</div>


# Full-spectrum informativeness

```{r fig_f4, fig.width=11, fig.height=11}
show_fig("F4_three_dimensions")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** Three properties of each bin side by side:

- **A**, how much change there is;
- **B**, how precisely it is estimated (bootstrap standard error; smaller = more precise);
- **C**, what percentage of recordings contain at least a minimal amount of time in that bin (> 0.25 min/day per 10 mg).

Panel C includes M0 as a reference.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- Precision (B) is worst at the lowest intensities, where day-to-day and between-patient variation in sedentary and light time is large, and becomes very good above ~150 mg.
- Coverage (C) is ~100% up to ~200 mg and then drops.
- Coverage is consistently higher at follow-up than at baseline in the high bins: at 260–280 mg, `r dv("qc_objects","coverage",list(kind="bins",visit_code="M0",descriptor="260-280",limit="0.25"),"pct_above")` % of recordings at M0 against `r dv("qc_objects","coverage",list(kind="bins",visit_code="M3",descriptor="260-280",limit="0.25"),"pct_above")` % at M3.

**Why it is interesting.**

- A larger share of follow-up recordings than of baseline recordings contains measurable time at high intensities. Note that coverage compares different sets of recordings at each visit, not the same patients.
- Coverage and precision are highest where most of the daily time is spent. This is a property of the time distribution, not evidence for a preferred intensity band.

</div>


```{r fig_f5, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
show_fig("F5_confidence_sets")
```

<div class="note-box">

**How to read.**

- **Black** bins are those where the change is positive *with simultaneous 95% confidence*.
- **Grey** bins are those where a positive change is plausible but not proven.
- **White** bins would be those where even a positive change is not supported.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- On the absolute scale the change is certainly positive over `r inner_set("E1","bins","M3")` at M3, `r inner_set("E1","bins","M6")` at M6 and `r inner_set("E1","bins","M18")` at M18.
- Requiring at least +0.5 min/day per 10 mg narrows this to `r inner_set("E1","bins","M3",0.5)` at M3 and `r inner_set("E1","bins","M6",0.5)` at M6.
- These ranges mark where the change is *certainly* positive. Their lower edge (about 80–90 mg) reflects precision as much as size: below it, gains of similar size are estimated too imprecisely. They are therefore not a recommended band.

</div>


## Shape of change (E3) {.unnumbered}

```{r fig_f3, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}
show_rev("rev_CD_objects", "C1")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows (explanation revised, A07-C; numbers unchanged).**

Each recording is treated as a 24-h composition of 21 parts: <20 mg, 19 bins from 20 to 300 mg, and ≥300 mg. For each part, the *centred log-ratio* (clr) is the log of its minutes minus the mean log over all 21 parts, i.e. its size **relative to the geometric mean of the whole day**. The figure plots the mean *paired change* in clr from M0 to each follow-up visit.

**Panel A — smooth redistribution.**

- **Points with shaded 95 % CI:** observed mean clr change per bin.
- **Dark curve:** the visit-specific smooth trend, a natural spline (df 3) in log intensity fitted separately for M3, M6 and M18 with an identical specification.
- **Positive values (grey area):** the bin takes a *larger share of the day* than at M0, relative to the other parts. **Negative values:** a smaller share.
- Because the clr is relative, a negative value does *not* mean fewer absolute minutes. Bins of 40–70 mg have negative clr change although their absolute minutes barely change (E1); they simply grow less than the rest of the day's activity.

**Panel B — localised departures.**

- **Line:** the residual, observed clr change minus the smooth trend.
- **Positive residual:** that bin gained *more* than the smooth trend predicts at its intensity. **Negative residual:** it gained less.
- **Shaded band:** the simultaneous 95 % band (max-t over the 19 bins of a visit; patient-level cluster bootstrap, B = 2000). It controls the chance of *any* false exceedance across the whole spectrum, not bin by bin.
- **Criteria for a localised departure** (all required): ≥ 2 adjacent bins with the band excluding 0; bounded on both sides by bins whose band includes 0; not at the grid edges; and the same result under every zero-replacement value, under ≥ 5 valid days, and after excluding the UCTD/SSc patient.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- **Panel A:** at every visit the curve rises smoothly from negative (low intensities lose share) to positive (high intensities gain share).
  - The share of the day spent below 20 mg falls (M3 clr change `r ev("E3_clr","composition","M3","<20",2)`).
  - The share above 300 mg rises (`r ev("E3_clr","composition","M3",">=300",2)`).
- **Panel B:** the residuals stay within the band everywhere, so there is no localised hump.

**Why it is interesting.**

- This is the central result. Within the resolution of the test, improvement in IIM looks like a **"tilt" of the whole activity profile**: low-intensity bins lose relative share and high-intensity bins gain it.
- No intensity range stands out beyond this smooth tilt.
- **Resolution of the test:** localised extra gains of about +22% (+0.2 log), 2–6 bins wide, would very likely have been detected. Smaller departures of about +10% may be missed, particularly at M18 (see the power table in the validation section).
- Clinically, this favours describing recovery with profile-based measures together with a volume measure, rather than with a single new threshold.

</div>

<div class="warning-box">

**What "no localised departure" does *not* mean.** The absence of a statistically supported hump does not establish that all intensity regions are clinically equally informative. Regions differ in how many minutes change (E1), in relative change (E2), in precision and coverage (F4) and in how widely the gain is shared (F6). The shape test only says that, at this resolution and sample size, no bin gains clearly more or less than a smooth tilt predicts.

</div>

### Is the E3 verdict robust to the bin grid and the smooth-null specification? (A07-C) {.unnumbered}

```{r fig_c2, fig.width=13, fig.height=10}
show_rev("rev_CD_objects", "C2")
```

```{r tab_variants}
if (has("rev_CD_objects")) {
  rev_CD_objects$var_decisions |>
    dplyr::transmute(Variant = variant, Class = class, Visit = visit, Bins = n_bins,
                     `Positive bumps` = positive_bumps, `Negative bumps` = negative_bumps,
                     `Bins with band excl. 0` = n_bins_band_excl0, Verdict = verdict) |>
    kbl_house("E3 bump rule under alternative smooth nulls and bin grids (matrix cluster bootstrap, B = 2000)", 0)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- **Why bin width cannot bias E3 directly.** Normalising per 10 mg multiplies every bin by a constant (10 / width), and the clr centre is a constant per recording. In a *paired change* both cancel or are absorbed by the spline intercept. The residuals are therefore identical whether minutes, minutes per 10 mg or clr values are used; the numerical difference is below 10⁻¹⁵ (validation R5b).
- **Two remaining routes for bin width.** Unequal widths affect (i) where the bins sit on the log-intensity axis, with 10 points in 20–120 mg and 9 in 120–300 mg, and (ii) how finely the spectrum is resolved.
- **Variants that test these routes:**
  - a fit that weights each bin by the log-intensity range it covers;
  - a uniform 20-mg grid (14 bins);
  - bounded bins up to 400 mg (23 bins).
  The last two change the resolution or range and therefore the estimand; they are robustness checks of the *conclusion*, not of the same number.
- **Smooth-null flexibility:** df = 1 (straight line), 2, 4 and 5 alongside the primary df = 3.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- With a smooth null of df ≥ 3, with width weighting and on both alternative grids, **no localised departure is flagged at any visit** (`r if (isTRUE(claim_ok("no bump under any df >= 3"))) "checked" else "[check]"`).
- Only the two least flexible nulls flag something: a *negative* run at 50–70 mg. The straight line (df 1) flags it at M6 and M18, df 2 only at M18.
  - This is the curvature of the S-shaped profile in panel A that a straight line or a df-2 spline cannot follow, the issue already identified in the original plan (R1).
  - The simulation below shows that df 2 raises false alarms in exactly this situation, at M18 in particular. These flags are therefore not evidence of a localised effect.

</div>

```{r fig_c3, fig.width=13, fig.height=8}
show_rev("rev_CD_objects", "C3")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** A plasmode simulation built from the patients' own paired clr changes (500 datasets × 1000 bootstrap replicates per cell) addresses three questions:

- **False alarms (top left).** The true population profile is the smooth df-3 fit with no bump. How often does the rule flag something when the test uses df 2–5?
- **Misspecification (top middle).** The same, but the true profile is the more flexible df-5 fit.
- **Power (remaining panels).** How often is a +10 % or +22 % (+0.1 / +0.2 log) bump injected on 2 bins (120–160 mg) or 6 bins (70–140 mg) detected in the right place?

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation — is df = 3 a reasonable choice?**

- **Calibration.** With df 3 the rule keeps false alarms well below 5 % when the truth is smooth (`r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) { x <- rev_CD_objects$df_sim_summary; x <- x[x$scenario == "null" & x$df_true == 3 & x$df_test == 3, ]; paste(sprintf("%s %.1f %%", x$visit, x$pct_any_bump), collapse = ", ") } else NA_TXT`). With df 2, false alarms rise to `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) { x <- rev_CD_objects$df_sim_summary; x <- x[x$scenario == "null" & x$df_true == 3 & x$df_test == 2, ]; paste(sprintf("%s %.1f %%", x$visit, x$pct_any_bump), collapse = ", ") } else NA_TXT`.
- **Power.** df 3 detects large bumps (+22 %) almost always, whether narrow or broad. With df 4–5 the spline itself starts to absorb broad bumps: detection of a 6-bin +22 % bump falls from about 100 % (df 3) to `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) { x <- rev_CD_objects$df_sim_summary; x <- x[x$scenario == "6 bins 70-140, +0.2" & x$df_test == 5, ]; paste0(fmt(min(x$pct_detected), 0), "–", fmt(max(x$pct_detected), 0)) } else NA_TXT` % (df 5).
- **df 4 is a credible alternative.** Under the df-3 null it is equally well calibrated (≤ 1 % false alarms) and detects *narrow* small bumps more often than df 3 (2 bins, +10 %: `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) { x <- rev_CD_objects$df_sim_summary; x <- x[x$scenario == "2 bins 120-160, +0.1" & x$df_test == 4, ]; paste(sprintf("%.0f", x$pct_detected), collapse = "/") } else NA_TXT` % vs `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) { x <- rev_CD_objects$df_sim_summary; x <- x[x$scenario == "2 bins 120-160, +0.1" & x$df_test == 3, ]; paste(sprintf("%.0f", x$pct_detected), collapse = "/") } else NA_TXT` % at M3/M6/M18), but loses broad bumps.
- **The simulation favours df 3 partly by design**, because its "true null" is the df-3 fit. If the true smooth profile were as wiggly as the df-5 fit, neither df 3 nor df 4 would be calibrated at M6 (false alarms `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) { x <- rev_CD_objects$df_sim_summary; x <- x[x$scenario == "null" & x$df_true == 5 & x$df_test %in% 3:4 & x$visit == "M6", ]; paste(sprintf("%.0f %% (df %d)", x$pct_any_bump, x$df_test), collapse = ", ") } else NA_TXT`). Such false alarms would create bumps, and none was observed, so this works against the observed conclusion rather than for it.
- **Conclusion.** df = 3 is retained as the pre-specified choice of the locked plan, with a reasonable balance of calibration and power for both narrow and broad bumps; it is not shown to be optimal. The substantive result does not depend on it: **df 3, 4 and 5 all give "no localised departure"**, and only the visibly too rigid df 1–2 nulls flag the 50–70 mg curvature.

</div>

```{r tab_decision}
} else if (has("primary_objects")) {

```

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- The verdict "no localised departure; smooth redistribution" is identical across all variants:
  - three choices of how zero minutes are handled;
  - restriction to ≥ 5 valid days;
  - exclusion of the patient with UCTD/SSc.
- The *linear tilt* (how strongly the profile rotates towards higher intensities) is positive at every visit:
  - largest at M3: `r ev("E3_slope","composition","M3","slope_per_log_mg",2)`;
  - smaller at M6 (`r ev("E3_slope","composition","M6","slope_per_log_mg",2)`) and M18 (`r ev("E3_slope","composition","M18","slope_per_log_mg",2)`).

</div>


## Heterogeneity and timing (C1, C3, C5) {.unnumbered}

```{r fig_f6, fig.width=12, fig.height=11}
show_rev("rev_AB_objects", "B1")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows (revised, A07-B).** Three different questions, kept apart; low (20–120 mg, left) and high intensities (120–400 mg, right) have separate axes:

- **A. Patients with a gain:** the percentage of patients whose time in the bin increased. 50 % (grey) is what random up/down fluctuation would give.
- **B. Concentration of positive gains:** the share of all positive gains contributed by the top 10 % of patients (k = ceiling(0.1 × pairs): 5 at M3, 6 at M6, 4 at M18). The grey line is the share if every patient with a gain gained exactly the same amount (about 13–30 %). This is the **smallest possible value**, not a realistic null: any real data lie above it. The informative part is *how far* above it, and how this compares across intensities and visits.
- **C. Net / gross index:** the sum of all changes divided by the sum of their absolute values. Values near 0 mean gains and losses cancel; 1 means everybody changes in the same direction.

Top 10 % are selected separately in every bin and visit; shaded = pointwise 95 % cluster-bootstrap CI.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- **How many patients gain.** From 70 mg upwards `r conc_range("pct_positive", 70, 400)` % of patients gain time in a bin, depending on bin and visit (for example M3, 260–280 mg: `r conc_ci("M3","260-280","pct_positive")` %). Below ~60 mg it is about half, i.e. no consistent direction.
- **How concentrated the gains are.** From 60 mg upwards the top 10 % contribute `r conc_range("share_pos", 60, 400)` % of the positive gains, i.e. 2.0–5.1 times the minimum possible value (equal gains).
  - Concentration is **of similar size across most of the spectrum** (`r conc_range("share_pos", 60, 200)` % at 60–200 mg across visits).
  - At M3 it is numerically **higher above ~240 mg** (`r conc_ci("M3","300-325","share_pos")` % at 300–325 mg); at M6 it is similar to M3 around 240–260 mg; at **M18** it stays at about 35 % across 70–400 mg. The visit and intensity differences rest on overlapping pointwise intervals and were not tested formally. Leaving out a single patient moves the share in a bin ≥ 240 mg by up to `r if (has("rev_validation_objects") && !is.null(rev_validation_objects$loo_b2)) fmt(max(rev_validation_objects$loo_b2$max_shift_share_pp), 1) else NA_TXT` percentage points (validation R7), so these high-intensity values depend on individual patients.
  - The highest shares are in the lowest bins (20–40 mg: `r conc_range("share_pos", 20, 40)` %), where only about half the patients gain and the net change is near zero; there the statistic describes noise rather than improvement.
  - Concentration in *absolute minutes* partly mirrors how unequal patients' baseline levels are: patients who already spend more time at an intensity can add more minutes there.
  - Summarised over all time above 100 mg, the top 10 % contribute `r conc_ci("M3","T100","share_pos")` % of the positive gains at M3, `r conc_ci("M6","T100","share_pos")` % at M6 and `r conc_ci("M18","T100","share_pos")` % at M18.
- **Gains and losses cancel at low intensities.** The net/gross index is near 0 below ~60 mg (panel C). This is why the original "share of the net gain" exploded there (below).

**What changed against the first report.**

- The first report stated that "above 200 mg, the 10 % of patients with the largest gains contribute 46–75 % of the total gain", read as a high-intensity *minority of strong responders*. That figure used the net gain as denominator. Above 200 mg the net/gross index is 0.49–0.85, so the net share there is only moderately higher than the positive-gain share; the problem of the net estimand is mainly in the low bins, where it becomes undefined or exceeds 100 %.
- With the positive-gain estimand the top 10 % account for about 32–65 % of positive gains, of similar size at moderate and high intensities. The data do not single out the high-intensity range as carried by a special minority.
- The revised reading: **change is broad in direction (most patients gain above 70 mg) and unequal in size, to a similar degree across the spectrum.**

**Caution.** Concentration of gains describes the *distribution* of change. It is not evidence of a biologically distinct responder subgroup: the same skewed pattern arises from continuous variation in response plus measurement noise, and the top 10 % need not be the same patients across bins. Bootstrap percentile intervals for "top-k" statistics are approximate; the independent review found their bias small (mean −0.4 percentage points).

</div>

```{r fig_f6_orig, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
show_rev("rev_AB_objects", "B2")
```

<div class="warning-box">

**Original estimand, kept for reproducibility.** The share of the *net* cohort gain contributed by the top 10 % (the first report's panel B) is reproduced exactly. It has two defects:

- It is **undefined** when the net change is ≤ 0. This is why the curves start at different intensities: M3 20–40 mg and M18 30–60 mg are missing.
- It **exceeds 100 %** (up to `r fmt(max(rev_AB_objects$conc$share_net_orig, na.rm = TRUE), 0)` % at M6, 30–40 mg) when gains and losses nearly cancel. Points marked × have a net/gross index below 0.20. This cut-off is a pragmatic flag: the net share can exceed 100 % whenever the index is below 1, so values near 100 % in "interpretable" cells (e.g. 60–80 mg) also mainly reflect cancellation.

Values above 100 % are not computational errors: the top 10 % gained more than the whole cohort's net gain, because other patients lost time.

</div>


```{r tab_c5}
if (has("descriptive_objects")) {
  descriptive_objects$c5 |>
    dplyr::transmute(Visit = visit, n, `Mean ΔIG` = mean_d_ig, `Mean Δ mean ENMO (mg)` = mean_d_enmo,
                     `Mean clr tilt` = mean_clr_slope, `Spearman tilt vs ΔIG` = spearman_slope_vs_d_ig,
                     `Spearman tilt vs Δ ENMO` = spearman_slope_vs_d_enmo) |>
    kbl_house("C5 — Is the change captured by a smooth tilt (intensity gradient)?")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- Whether the patient-level "tilt" of the profile (from E3) moves together with established summary metrics: the change in intensity gradient (ΔIG) and the change in mean acceleration (Δ mean ENMO).
- A Spearman correlation of 1 would mean they carry identical information.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- The tilt correlates moderately with ΔIG (ρ ≈ `r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M6"),"spearman_slope_vs_d_ig",2)` at M6) and less strongly with Δ mean ENMO (ρ ≈ `r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M6"),"spearman_slope_vs_d_enmo",2)`).
- Mean ENMO rose by about `r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M6"),"mean_d_enmo",1)` mg at M6.

- The two measures diverge at group level: mean ΔIG *increases* from M3 to M18 (`r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M3"),"mean_d_ig",3)` → `r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M18"),"mean_d_ig",3)`), while the clr tilt *decreases* (`r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M3"),"mean_clr_slope",3)` → `r dv("descriptive_objects","c5",list(visit="M18"),"mean_clr_slope",3)`).
- A plausible reason is that GGIR computes IG over a wider range (0–4000 mg in 25-mg bins) than this analysis (20–400 mg).

**Why it is interesting.**

- IG is a closely related, cut-point-free summary of the same tilt. Both are slopes of log time against log intensity, so some correlation is expected by construction.
- A ρ of about 0.7 means the two share only about half of the between-patient ranking, and their time courses differ.
- IG is therefore a reasonable but **not equivalent** summary.
- For studies in IIM, a combination of a volume measure (mean ENMO or time above a conventional threshold) and IG is well justified. The spectrum profile is the more detailed descriptive complement.

</div>

```{r fig_f7, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
show_fig("F7_subtype_profiles")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- Three pre-specified summaries per subtype:
  - change in time above 100 mg (mean, median with IQR, % of patients with a gain);
  - the patient-level clr tilt;
  - the change in IG.
- F7 shows the full bin-by-bin relative profile per subtype.
- Purely descriptive: no CIs and no tests, 12–18 pairs per subtype and visit.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- The summaries differ in size between DM, IMNM and ASyS.
- Within each subtype, medians and IQRs show wide individual variation, so a small mean does not mean that no patient improved.

**Why it is interesting.**

- Differences in recovery of daily activity between myositis subtypes are clinically plausible. With these sample sizes, however, any difference could be due to chance, to baseline severity, disease duration or treatment.
- A pre-specified, adequately powered subtype analysis adjusted for these factors is a natural next study.

</div>

<div class="warning-box">

**Caution:** No inference about subtype effects should be drawn from this table or figure. Any single bin or subtype highlighted after looking at the data would be a post-hoc selection.

</div>

### Subtypes adjusted for baseline severity (A07-E, exploratory) {.unnumbered}

<div class="note-box">

**Data source.** Baseline clinical variables are not part of the locked master dataset. They come from `klinicka_data_12102026.xlsx`; the md5 of the file is stored in the log of script 09. All `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) rev_E_objects$linkage$master_patients else NA_TXT` patients link to it, and the subtype codes agree for every patient with a code in both sources.

</div>

```{r tab_e_avail}
if (has("rev_E_objects")) {
  rev_E_objects$availability |>
    dplyr::transmute(Subtype = subtype, Patients = patients, `With M0 recording` = with_M0_recording,
                     `With ≥ 1 follow-up pair` = with_follow_up_pair, `… and ph_VAS` = pairs_with_ph_vas,
                     `… and MMT8` = pairs_with_mmt8, `… and FI2` = pairs_with_fi2) |>
    kbl_house("Availability of baseline severity indicators (M0) among patients with a follow-up pair", 0)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

```{r tab_e_dist}
if (has("rev_E_objects")) {
  rev_E_objects$distributions |>
    dplyr::transmute(Subtype = subtype, `ph_VAS (mm)` = ph_vas, `MDAAT muscle VAS` = muscle_vas,
                     `Extramuscular VAS` = extramuscular_vas, `MMT8 (0–80)` = mmt8, FI2 = fi2, HAQ = haq,
                     `Disease duration (y)` = disease_duration, `GC (mg/day)` = gc_mg_day) |>
    kbl_house("Baseline severity by subtype: median [IQR] (n), patients with a follow-up pair")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

```{r tab_e_construct}
if (has("rev_E_objects")) {
  rev_E_objects$construct |>
    dplyr::transmute(Subtype = subtype, n, `ρ ph_VAS – muscle VAS` = rho_phvas_muscle,
                     `ρ ph_VAS – extramuscular VAS` = rho_phvas_extramuscular, `ρ ph_VAS – MMT8` = rho_phvas_mmt8,
                     `Median muscle VAS` = median_muscle_vas, `Median extramuscular VAS` = median_extramuscular_vas) |>
    kbl_house("What does ph_VAS measure in each subtype? (Spearman correlations at M0)")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="finding-box">

**Is ph_VAS a suitable measure of initial disease activity for this question?**

- Physician global activity (ph_VAS) summarises *all* disease activity: muscle, skin, lung, joints and constitutional symptoms. What drives it differs by subtype:
  - in **IMNM** it is almost purely muscle activity (ρ with muscle VAS `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$construct$rho_phvas_muscle[rev_E_objects$construct$subtype == "IMNM"]) else NA_TXT`; median extramuscular VAS ≈ 2 mm);
  - in **DM** and **ASyS** it is substantially driven by extramuscular activity (ρ with extramuscular VAS `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) paste(fmt(rev_E_objects$construct$rho_phvas_extramuscular[rev_E_objects$construct$subtype %in% c("DM","ASyS")]), collapse = " and ") else NA_TXT`, vs `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) paste(fmt(rev_E_objects$construct$rho_phvas_muscle[rev_E_objects$construct$subtype %in% c("DM","ASyS")]), collapse = " and ") else NA_TXT` with muscle VAS; n = 14–18) and is practically unrelated to muscle strength (ρ with MMT8 ≈ 0).
- The same ph_VAS value therefore means **less muscle impairment in DM/ASyS than in IMNM**. As an adjustment for "how impaired was the patient's mobility at the start", ph_VAS is imperfect and differentially so across subtypes. MMT8 is the more direct measure of muscle impairment, which is why it is used as a sensitivity analysis.
- **Collinearity.** ph_VAS barely differs between subtypes (R² on subtype `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$vif_sev$r2_on_subtype[1], 2) else NA_TXT`, VIF `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$vif_sev$vif[1], 2) else NA_TXT`). MMT8 is lower in IMNM (R² `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$vif_sev$r2_on_subtype[2], 2) else NA_TXT`, VIF `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$vif_sev$vif[2], 2) else NA_TXT`). MMT8 and FI2 are strongly correlated (ρ = `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$collinearity$fi2[rev_E_objects$collinearity$variable == "mmt8"]) else NA_TXT` in the analysis sample), so FI2 is not added to MMT8 models; FI2 also has the most missing values.

</div>

```{r fig_e1, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}
show_rev("rev_E_objects", "E1")
```

```{r tab_e_lrt}
if (has("rev_E_objects")) {
  rev_E_objects$lrt |>
    dplyr::transmute(Outcome = outcome, Severity = ifelse(severity == "ph_vas", "ph_VAS", "MMT8"), Test = test,
                     `χ²` = chisq, df, p, Patients = n_patients, Observations = n_obs) |>
    kbl_house("Likelihood-ratio tests (ML, random intercept; exploratory, unadjusted for multiplicity)", 3)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- Models of the change from M0 at M3, M6 and M18 for three pre-specified summaries; no single bin is selected:
  - ΔT100 (min/day above 100 mg);
  - the patient-level clr tilt (the "shape" summary);
  - ΔIG (change in intensity gradient).
- DM is the reference. Contrasts are evaluated at average severity, shown per visit and averaged over visits ("mean M3-M18"), with 95 % patient-level cluster-bootstrap intervals (B = 2000).
- How to read the rows of the figure:
  - **row 1:** unadjusted, all subtype patients;
  - **row 2:** unadjusted, restricted to patients with ph_VAS. Comparing rows 1 and 2 shows what the *sample restriction* alone does;
  - **rows 3–5:** adjusted for ph_VAS; + ph_VAS × visit; + baseline value of the outcome;
  - **row 6:** adjusted for MMT8 instead of ph_VAS.
- About 12–18 patients per subtype and visit.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation (exploratory).**

- **ΔT100 — IMNM gains less time above 100 mg than DM.** Averaged over visits the difference is `r ev_rev("dT100","E_a_unadjusted","none","all subtype patients","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)` min/day unadjusted.
  - It is practically unchanged by restricting the sample and by adjusting for ph_VAS: `r ev_rev("dT100","E_b_sev","ph_vas","complete ph_vas","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)`. The global test of any subtype effect gives p = `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$lrt$p[rev_E_objects$lrt$outcome == "dT100" & rev_E_objects$lrt$severity == "ph_vas" & rev_E_objects$lrt$test == "any subtype effect (main + interaction)"], 3) else NA_TXT`.
  - In the MMT8 sample the point estimate is nearly the same unadjusted (`r ev_rev("dT100","E_a_unadjusted","mmt8","complete mmt8","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)`) and adjusted for MMT8 (`r ev_rev("dT100","E_b_sev","mmt8","complete mmt8","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM",1)`); the interval widens to include 0 and the global subtype test is p = `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$lrt$p[rev_E_objects$lrt$outcome == "dT100" & rev_E_objects$lrt$severity == "mmt8" & rev_E_objects$lrt$test == "any subtype effect (main + interaction)"], 3) else NA_TXT`. MMT8 itself is not associated with ΔT100 (likelihood-ratio p = `r if (has("rev_E_objects")) fmt(rev_E_objects$lrt$p[rev_E_objects$lrt$outcome == "dT100" & rev_E_objects$lrt$severity == "mmt8" & rev_E_objects$lrt$test == "severity main effect"], 2) else NA_TXT`).
  - The data therefore do **not** show that baseline muscle weakness explains the smaller IMNM gain; the MMT8-adjusted contrast is just less precise. ASyS and DM do not differ.
- **Shape of change (tilt) and ΔIG — no evidence of subtype differences, with wide intervals** (e.g. tilt IMNM − DM `r ev_rev("tilt","E_b_sev","ph_vas","complete ph_vas","mean M3-M18","IMNM - DM")`). In all patients, unadjusted, ASyS gains slightly less IG than IMNM (`r ev_rev("dIG","E_a_unadjusted","none","all subtype patients","mean M3-M18","ASyS - IMNM",3)`); restricting to the ph_VAS sample already moves the interval over 0, and adjustment shrinks it further. There is no subtype × visit interaction for any outcome (all p > 0.05).
- **Baseline severity and the shape of change.** Patients with higher baseline ph_VAS show a *larger* tilt towards higher intensities; for MMT8 the association points the same way (weaker muscles → larger ΔIG; likelihood-ratio p < 0.05) but its bootstrap interval includes 0:
  - tilt per 10 mm ph_VAS: `r ev_rev("tilt","E_b_sev","ph_vas","complete ph_vas","all","severity (per unit)")`;
  - ΔIG per 10 mm ph_VAS: `r ev_rev("dIG","E_b_sev","ph_vas","complete ph_vas","all","severity (per unit)",3)`;
  - ΔIG per 5 MMT8 points: `r ev_rev("dIG","E_b_sev","mmt8","complete mmt8","all","severity (per unit)",3)`.
  This is compatible with more room to improve, or with regression to the mean. For ΔIG the association weakens when the baseline IG is added. A severity × visit interaction is not supported.

**How to use this.**

- These are hypothesis-generating estimates: three outcomes, two severity measures and several models, with no multiplicity control and 12–18 patients per cell.
- Likelihood-ratio tests with ML fits on about 47 patients are somewhat anti-conservative; where they disagree with the bootstrap intervals (e.g. MMT8 → ΔIG), the bootstrap is the more cautious guide. In model E_c the severity coefficient refers to M3 (reference visit of the severity × visit term).
- The IMNM-vs-DM difference in *volume* (ΔT100) is the one signal worth testing in an independent cohort, ideally with baseline muscle strength pre-specified as a covariate. Disease duration and glucocorticoid dose are listed but not modelled, to avoid over-fitting.
- None of this identifies a biologically distinct responder subgroup.

</div>


### Does the shape of change differ between follow-up visits? (A07-D) {.unnumbered}

The C1 table above (M6 − M3, bin by bin, original analysis) is reproduced exactly by the revision code (validation R9b). The revision adds formal paired comparisons for all three visit pairs.

```{r fig_d1, fig.width=15, fig.height=10}
show_rev("rev_CD_objects", "D1")
```

```{r tab_shape}
if (has("rev_CD_objects")) {

    dplyr::transmute(Contrast = contrast, Sample = sample, Patients = n_patients,
                     `Tilt difference (95% CI)` = paste0(fmt(slope_diff), " (", fmt(slope_ci_low), " to ", fmt(slope_ci_high), ")"),
                     `Tilt p (Holm)` = paste0(fmt(slope_p_boot, 3), " (", fmt(slope_p_holm, 3), ")"),
                     `Smooth-curve Wald (3 df)` = fmt(wald_3df, 1),
                     `Smooth p boot (Holm)` = paste0(fmt(p_wald_boot, 3), " (", fmt(p_wald_boot_holm, 3), ")"),
                     `Bins outside simult. band` = n_bins_band_excl0) |>
    kbl_house("Paired comparison of the shape of change between follow-up visits (cluster bootstrap, B = 2000)")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- **Panel A (descriptive only):** the three visit-specific smooth trends from F3 overlaid. They are based on different sets of patients (`r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) paste(c("M3","M6","M18"), sapply(c("M3","M6","M18"), \(v) unique(rev_CD_objects$smooth_curves$n_pairs[rev_CD_objects$smooth_curves$visit == v])), sep = " n = ", collapse = ", ") else NA_TXT` pairs), so visual differences can reflect who attended as well as how they changed.
- **Panel B and table:** the formal test. Within the same patients (M0 plus both visits), the difference "later minus earlier" clr change is analysed in three ways:
  - bin by bin, with a simultaneous band;
  - as the difference in linear *tilt*;
  - as a 3-df test that the smooth difference curve is flat, i.e. that the *shape* within 20–300 mg is the same apart from a constant shift (a constant shift, reflecting exchange with the <20 and ≥300 mg parts, is deliberately not tested).
- P-values are Holm-adjusted over the three pairs. A sensitivity analysis repeats everything in the `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) rev_CD_objects$n_all4 else NA_TXT` patients with all four visits.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- **Panel A looks different between visits:**
  - M3 is nearly a straight tilt that keeps rising to 300 mg;
  - M6 and M18 bend and flatten above ~175 mg.
- **The formal tests do not confirm a difference after multiplicity control:**
  - **Tilt:** no visit pair differs (M6 − M3: `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","slope_diff")`, 95 % CI `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","slope_ci_low")` to `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","slope_ci_high")`; all Holm p ≥ `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) fmt(min(rev_CD_objects$shape_summary$slope_p_holm[grepl("^all", rev_CD_objects$shape_summary$sample)]), 2) else NA_TXT`).
  - **Overall shape:** M6 vs M3 shows a nominal curvature difference (p = `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","p_wald_boot",3)`, Holm `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","p_wald_boot_holm",3)`; in the common sample p = `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","p_wald_boot",3,"common")`, Holm `r shape_v("M6 minus M3","p_wald_boot_holm",3,"common")`, i.e. borderline). M18 vs M3 gives p = `r shape_v("M18 minus M3","p_wald_boot",3)` (Holm `r shape_v("M18 minus M3","p_wald_boot_holm",3)`), and M18 vs M6 shows no difference (p = `r shape_v("M18 minus M6","p_wald_boot",3)`).
  - **Bin by bin:** no bin falls outside the simultaneous band in any comparison.
- **Conclusion.** The flatter high-intensity end at M6/M18 compared with M3 is a **descriptive pattern compatible with an early burst that consolidates**, not a statistically supported difference between recovery phases. The M18 − M3 point estimates in the 250–300 mg range (−0.2 to −0.3) are large but imprecise (34 patients).

</div>

```{r tab_timing}
if (has("rev_CD_objects")) {
  rev_CD_objects$timing |>
    dplyr::transmute(Contrast = contrast, Patients = n_patients,
                     `Earlier visit: months from M0, median (range)` = paste0(fmt(months_a_median, 1), " (", months_a_range, ")"),
                     `Later visit: months from M0, median (range)` = paste0(fmt(months_b_median, 1), " (", months_b_range, ")"),
                     `Gap, median months` = fmt(gap_months_median, 1),
                     `Same season, earlier vs later (%)` = fmt(pct_same_season_a_b, 0),
                     `Same season as M0, earlier (%)` = fmt(pct_same_season_M0_a, 0),
                     `Same season as M0, later (%)` = fmt(pct_same_season_M0_b, 0)) |>
    kbl_house("Timing and season of the compared visits")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="warning-box">

**Why visit differences cannot be separated from time of year and timing.**

- **Season.** Almost no patient is recorded in the same season at M0 and at any follow-up: 0 % at M6 and M18, a few % at M3. The M3 → M6 comparison almost always crosses seasons (`r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) fmt(rev_CD_objects$timing$pct_same_season_a_b[1], 0) else NA_TXT` % same season), whereas M6 and M18 fall in the same season in `r if (has("rev_CD_objects")) fmt(rev_CD_objects$timing$pct_same_season_a_b[3], 0) else NA_TXT` % of patients. Season is therefore tied to the visit by design and cannot be adjusted for in the shape contrasts.
- **Timing.** M3 (2–6 months) and M6 (5–9 months) overlap in actual time since baseline. "M3 vs M6" means *early vs later follow-up*, not exact time points.
- **Who attends.** The pairs differ in who is included; the common-sample analysis gives a similar, slightly stronger but still Holm-non-significant M6-vs-M3 signal. Patients without M0 are excluded for consistency with E3, although M0 cancels in the visit difference.

</div>

# Robustness, validation results and discrepancy log {.tabset}

## Sensitivity analyses {.unnumbered}

```{r tab_sens}
if (has("sensitivity_objects")) {
  sensitivity_objects$compare_summary |>
    dplyr::transmute(Estimand = estimand, Block = block, Sensitivity = sensitivity, n,
                     `Same sign as primary (%)` = pct_same_sign, `Within primary 95% CI (%)` = pct_within_primary_ci) |>
    kbl_house("Agreement of sensitivity analyses with the primary E1/E2 estimates", 1)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- Under alternative analyses the estimates keep their direction in 94–100% of bins and stay within the primary 95% CI in 100% of bins. The alternatives are complete pairs only, a simpler random-intercept model, ≥ 5 valid days, and exclusion of the UCTD/SSc patient.
- **The main results are consistent under these analytic choices.** Containment within the primary CI is weak evidence, because all variants share most of the data.

</div>


```{r tab_anchor}
if (has("sensitivity_objects")) {
  kbl_house(sensitivity_objects$s5_anchor, "Seasonality anchor test (joint 2-df LRT of annual harmonics, corrected)", 3)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** A test of whether time of year (an annual sine/cosine cycle) explains part of the activity level. It is run for time above 100 mg and for the 100–110 mg bin.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- There is no evidence of a seasonal effect (p ≈ `r dv("sensitivity_objects","s5_anchor",list(descriptor="T100"),"LR_p",2)`). Season-adjusted models gave virtually the same visit effects.
- The previously empty seasonality sheet in A04/A07 was caused by a coding error that is now fixed.

</div>

<div class="warning-box">

**Caution:** Visits are tied to the calendar: no M0→M6 pair falls in the same season. Seasonal and treatment effects therefore cannot be fully separated, and a null seasonal test does not exclude a modest seasonal contribution.

</div>


```{r tab_tipping}
if (has("sensitivity_objects")) {
  sensitivity_objects$s9 |> dplyr::filter(block == "bins") |> dplyr::distinct(descriptor, n_with_m0, n_m18_imputed, tipping_delta) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tipping_ci = vapply(descriptor, \(d) as.numeric(tip_lo("bins", d, raw = TRUE)), numeric(1))) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Bin = descriptor, `Patients with M0` = n_with_m0, `M18 imputed` = n_m18_imputed,
                     `δ: point estimate → 0` = tipping_delta, `δ: lower 95% bound → 0` = tipping_ci) |>
    kbl_house("S9 — How much worse would missing M18 values have to be to remove the M0→M18 gain?")
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- Roughly 4 in 10 patients with a baseline have no M18 recording.
- The tipping point is how much *worse* their unobserved M18 values would have to be, compared with what the model predicts, before the M0→M18 gain disappears.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- For the *point estimate* to reach zero, the missing patients would have to have lost about 1.6 times what the observed patients gained. That ratio is fixed by the share of missing M18 data (24 of 63), so it is not informative on its own.
- The more relevant question is when the M18 gain stops being *statistically supported*: when the lower 95% bound reaches zero.
  - For 90–100 mg this happens at a shift of only about `r tip_lo("bins","90-100")` min/day per 10 mg in the missing patients.
  - For time above 100 mg it happens at about `r tip_lo("cumulative","T100")` min/day.
- These are modest shifts. Possible reasons for worse outcomes in non-attenders include relapse, hospitalisation or ILD progression, so **the M18 result is sensitive to plausible departures from MAR**. Reasons for missing visits should be collected.

</div>


## Validation (PASS/WARN/FAIL) {.unnumbered}

```{r tab_val}
if (has("validation_objects")) {
  validation_objects$validation_table |> dplyr::transmute(ID = id, Check = check, Status = status, Detail = detail) |>
    kbl_house("Validation plan results")
} else cat("*Table not available — run 06_VALIDATION_BOTH.R.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.** Automatic checks of the computations:

- arithmetic identities;
- reproducibility (the same result on 1 or many CPU cores);
- model convergence (all models converged);
- residual distribution;
- influence of single patients.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- All technical checks pass.
- Residuals are skewed (WARN), which is expected for minutes-per-day data. This is why all confidence intervals come from the patient bootstrap, not from model formulas.
- No single patient shifts any estimate by more than about one standard error.

</div>


```{r tab_power}
if (has("validation_objects")) {
  validation_objects$power_summary |>
    dplyr::transmute(Scenario = scenario, Visit = visit, Simulations = n_sim,
                     `Any bump flagged (%)` = pct_any_bump, `Injected bump detected (%)` = pct_detected) |>
    kbl_house("Plasmode power of the E3 bump rule (+0.2 log bump injected at follow-up)", 0)
} else cat("*Table not available.*\n")
```

<div class="note-box">

**What it shows.**

- A simulation answering: *if there were a special intensity band, would we have found it, and how often does the rule raise a false alarm?*
- **True null:** each patient's paired change was adjusted so that the population has the observed smooth tilt but no localised departure. Patients were then resampled and the decision rule applied.
- **Bump scenarios:** an extra +10% or +22% (+0.1 / +0.2 log) was added to 2, 3, 4 or 6 adjacent bins. A bump counts as detected only when the flagged region overlaps the injected bins.
- Monte-Carlo 95% intervals are given for each percentage.

</div>

<div class="finding-box">

**Evaluation.**

- **False alarms under the true null:** `r null_txt()`. A calibrated rule keeps these at or below the nominal 5%.
- **Large departures (+22%) are detected reliably**, narrow or broad:
  - 2 bins at 120–160 mg: `r pow_range("2 bins 120-160, +0.2")` %;
  - 3 bins at 180–240 mg: `r pow_range("3 bins 180-240, +0.2")` %;
  - 4 bins at 80–120 mg: `r pow_range("4 bins 80-120, +0.2")` %;
  - 6 bins at 70–140 mg: `r pow_range("6 bins 70-140, +0.2")` %.
- **Small departures (+10%) are detected less reliably**, and least at M18 (n = 39):
  - 2 bins: `r pow_range("2 bins 120-160, +0.1")` %;
  - 4 bins: `r pow_range("4 bins 80-120, +0.1")` %;
  - 6 bins: `r pow_range("6 bins 70-140, +0.1")` %.
  - For broad small humps the smooth null absorbs part of the departure.
- **The rule does not over-detect**: false alarms stayed at or below the nominal 5%, including at M18 (n = 39). This calibrates the bump rule. It does not by itself verify the coverage of every individual simultaneous band.
- **Conclusion on scope:** the absence of a localised band is well supported for departures of about +22% or more. Departures of about +10%, particularly broad ones or at M18, cannot be excluded, and when flagged they may be mislocalised: for a +10% 6-bin bump, *some* bump was flagged more often than the flag overlapped the injected bins.

</div>
